title: Potsdam to host new Europa Nostra Heritage Hub with a focus on climate resilience, civic engagement and youth capacity-building
content:
The State Capital City of Potsdam has entered into a strategic partnership with Europa Nostra, leading European heritage civil society network. On 29 October 2026, a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Potsdam was signed at the Old Town Hall by Potsdam’s Lord Mayor Noosha Aubel, the Secretary-General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the President of Europa Nostra Germany, Dr. Uwe Koch. From 2027 onwards, the Hub in Potsdam will prioritise climate-resilient cultural heritage management, civic engagement and, above all, capacity-building for young people.

The new Hub brings together Potsdam’s local expertise and Europa Nostra’s transnational network. The Palaces and Parks of Potsdam, which are inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List, and the city itself serve as a real-world laboratory for the conservation of cultural landscapes in the context of climate change. To this end, close collaboration with local institutions, such as the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) and the Research Centre Sanssouci (RECS), is foreseen.
